Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Zenith Insurance Group Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Zenith Insurance Group's Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me on the call today are Sarah Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Underwriting Officer; David Kim, Chief Investment Officer; Jennifer Lee, Chief Operating Officer; and Robert Hayes, Chief Claims Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we are making today may be considered forward-looking. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause our actual results to differ materially from those projected. We encourage you to review our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks and uncertainties.

I will now turn the call over to Sarah Thompson.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I'm pleased to report on Zenith Insurance Group's performance for Q3 2024. We delivered strong results, driven by disciplined underwriting that kept our combined ratio at our best third-quarter mark since 2019, meaningful improvements in customer acquisition efficiencies across our lines, prudent reinsurance recoveries bolstering our balance sheet, steady premium growth momentum, savvy capital deployment into high-return opportunities, and solid investment returns amid a dynamic market. We are making significant progress on our digital transformation initiatives, including AI enhancements in underwriting and claims that are already yielding tangible benefits.

Michael Chen, our CFO, will now provide a more detailed review of our financial performance.

Michael Chen: Thank you, Sarah. Good morning, everyone. As Sarah mentioned, we had a solid quarter. Our net income was $450 million, or $1.85 per share. Key drivers of our financial performance included robust net premiums earned up 8.2% year-over-year to $14.7 billion, favorable prior-year reserve development, higher investment yields from reinvestments, reinsurance inflows that cushioned catastrophe impacts, and ongoing expense discipline. Our combined ratio was 94.8%. Investment income for the quarter was $650 million. We continue to maintain a strong capital position, with an RBC ratio of 520%. Our expense ratio also improved to 27.9%.

Let me dive deeper into some of these highlights, starting with our combined ratio and forward guidance, which remains the cornerstone of our property and casualty underwriting discipline. It's the sum of our loss and loss adjustment expense ratio and underwriting expense ratio, expressed as a percentage of earned premiums. A sub-100% ratio signals profitable underwriting, and we've held that line even with elevated catastrophe activity. For Q4 2024, we're guiding to a combined ratio of 96.5% to 98.5%, which implies underwriting profit of $150 million to $250 million on projected earned premiums of $3.2 billion. This accounts for a seasonally softer quarter with expected catastrophe losses of $200 million to $250 million pretax, or 6 to 8 points, mainly from California wildfires and potential Northeast winter storms—similar to the $180 million from Atmospheric River events in Q4 2023. Excluding cats, our core loss ratio stays in the mid-62s, aided by about 1.5 points of favorable prior-year reserve development, particularly in auto physical damage within our commercial auto book. Social inflation trends are stabilizing too, with jury awards in liability lines up just 4% year-over-year compared to 12% in 2022.

On the expense side, we're guiding to 28.5% to 28.8%, a modest uptick from Q3's 27.9% due to higher variable commissions on premium growth and ramp-up in our AI-driven claims platform. But we've offset that with vendor consolidation and offshore processing, staying below our long-term 28% target. Regionally, our U.S. P&C operations, 65% of the book, should deliver around 95%, backed by 8.5% earned rate increases in personal lines auto and 7% in commercial multi-peril. Europe, 20% of premiums, faces pressure from €1.5 billion in flood claims in Germany and the Benelux, pushing ex-U.S. to 99%, but facultative reinsurance with partners like Swiss Re limits the hit to 2 points ceded. Asia-Pacific, our 10% share, benefits from premium growth in workers' comp via a new telematics-integrated product in Australia—modeled after Progressive's Snapshot—and holds at 93%.

For full-year 2025, we're introducing combined ratio guidance of 96.0% to 98.0%, setting us up for a fifth straight year of sub-100% profitability and $1.2 billion in aggregate P&C profits. This assumes 7-9% earned premium growth to $13.5 billion, flat accident-year ex-CAT loss ratio at 62.5%, and expense compression to 28.0% via scale. Key enablers include 6-8% rate adequacy across lines, especially in hardening excess and surplus markets where our Zenith E&S platform grows premiums 15%. We're non-renewing $400 million in underperforming middle-market property in wildfire-prone California, shifting to Gulf Coast habitational with mitigation credits, much like Chubb's wind pool approach. Our $150 million Zenith Nexus platform—a generative AI underwriting engine partnering with Palantir and Guidewire—is delivering 20% faster quotes and 5-point loss ratio gains in personal lines homeowners via predictive modeling. In auto, usage-based insurance with IoT telematics cuts frequency 12% in high-risk youth segments, contributing 1-2 points of annual improvement.

Reinsurance helps too: After our 1/1/25 renewal, we're ceding 25% net after the first $500 million layer—up from 22%—at good terms with 32% ceding commissions amid soft pricing. This protects against tail risks like a 1-in-100-year hurricane season, per RMS models costing the industry $150 billion. Industry context: ISO data shows 99.2% YTD averages amid 15% claims inflation, but peers like Travelers at 97.1% and Hartford at 98.4% affirm our sub-98% goal. Downside risks are higher severe convective storm activity up 30% per NOAA or labor strikes in workers' comp; upside from mild weather or more reserves.

Shifting to customer acquisition cost trends, or CAC—a vital gauge of our growth discipline in a competitive P&C landscape. Our blended CAC, covering direct marketing, commissions, digital ads, leads, and sales expenses, hit $312 per new policy in Q3, down 7.2% year-over-year from $336. That's six straight quarters of improvement from digital maturation and segmentation.

By segment: Personal lines—auto and homeowners, 55% of new business—saw CAC drop 12% to $185 from $210. Digital channels now 62% of new auto policies, up from 48%, with programmatic ads on Google DV360 and The Trade Desk cutting CPA to $42 from $58 via ML models on 150+ behavioral signals, including telematics from our SafeDrive app. Over 40% of new autos bundle UBI like Progressive's Snapshot but with edge AI for instant quotes, lowering CAC 18% for adopters and lifting retention 15%—our LTV:CAC at 4.8x beats Bain's 3.5x industry mark. U.S. personal CAC fell 14% amid Geico and Lemonade rivalry, using zip-level cat models for dynamic pricing; Europe dipped 6% despite GDPR, offset by Vodafone embedded auto acquiring 25,000 policies at $160 CAC.

Commercial P&C, 35% of new premiums, rose 3% to $728 from broker commissions at 18% versus 15%. Excluding mid-market, it fell 5% to $610 via our small business portal with 1,200 MGA APIs and Swiss Re links, cutting sales cycles 22% and SMB CAC to $420 like Next Insurance. Risk-adjusted, LTV:CAC holds 3.2x in high-margin construction and hospitality amid 8% premium hikes. North America up 2% from wildfire and hurricane renewals; Asia-Pacific down 9% to $550 via Ping An JV and WeChat mini-apps for SME quoting, leveraging China's 35% digital penetration.

Group life and health, 10%, plunged 22% to $245 per enrollee via embedded benefits in 150+ payroll platforms like ADP and Workday, delivering 35% of groups at $28 CPA versus $95 field sales. AI propensity scoring on 5 million claims hits 87% accuracy, cutting waste 30%. U.K. and Australia sub-$200 CAC yields 5.1x LTV:CAC.

Enterprise-wide, $250 million in cloud CRM like Salesforce Einstein and CDP like Treasure Data drove 15% CAC cuts via omnichannel. Multi-touch attribution shifted 40% of our $1.2 billion marketing to CTV and retail media. Macro helps: Inflation lifts ratios but supports 6-8% growth; rates boost yields to 4.2%. We're targeting sub-$300 blended CAC by 2024-end, 4.2x LTV:CAC via GenAI personalization (25% auto conversion lift), embedded fintech ties like Affirm PAYD home, and 88% retention cross-sells. Q4 expects 4-6% sequential drop, risks broker inflation or ad fatigue mitigated by first-party data.

On premium growth guidance: Full-year 2024 now 7% to 9% net, up from 6-8%, on strong retention and new business. Q4 at 5-7%, seasonal but rate-driven. P&C leads at 8-10%: Commercial 9-11% on 5.5% Q3 rates and 91% retention, SME new business +12%; personal 6-8% via DriveSafe telematics on 2.5 million policies improving loss ratios 15%. Life & health 5-7%, annuities $1.2 billion Q3; cyber/D&O +15%. U.S. 8-10% on Florida/Midwest rates; Europe 4-6% offset by Germany/France E&S; Asia 10-12% post-Singapore InsurTech stake like Bowtie. Drivers: 4-6% 2025 rates vs. 3.2% trends, 90.5% retention +20% rounding, AI underwriting cutting reviews 40%, embedded via Shopify $500 million ARP. Reinsurance renewals +5% commissions, $2 billion cat protection for 58-60% attritional losses. Prioritizing profitable growth, ROE 14%+; risks competition, La Niña cats, 4% repair inflation.

Investment performance featured net realized gains of $178 million, up 25% QoQ from tactical fixed income sales—$145 million on corporates in financials/industrials—and $33 million equities like tech mirroring NVIDIA. Minor $12 million OTTI on high-yield. Unrealized losses $325 million widened AOCI to $2.1 billion (0.5% assets), from rates to 4.75% hitting $320 billion fixed income ($280 million loss) and equities ($45 million). Total return 2.1%, beating Bloomberg by 80 bps; YTD NII +12% to $4.2 billion on 5.1% reinvestments. U.S. 65% harvested curve steepening; Europe 20% losses from ECB/energy; Asia 10% JGB gains offset China ABS cuts. Initiatives: $10 billion alts shift ($4 billion private credit), derivatives hedging 40% equity, $50 billion ESG fixed at 4.5% yields. Forward: Gains accelerate on pruning $5-7 billion at 5%+; 92% IG quality.

Reinsurance recoveries: Q3 $1.2 billion received, +35% YoY, 92% of gross cats ceded, adding 420 bps to ratio for 58.4% underlying. From Hurricane Idalia $428 million (95% recovery Swiss Re/Munich Re), Maui wildfires $320 million, casualty $150 million. 12-month rate 94% vs. 88% FY2022 via RMS v18.1 PML modeling. Outstanding $3.8 billion: $2.1 billion H2 2024 ($950 million U.S. cats), $1.7 billion 2025. North America +12% over expect; Asia slower on Typhoon Yagi now 85%; EMEA steady. AI portal cuts cycles 38%, digitized bordereaux -25% disputes; new casualty aggregate, parametric pilots $75 million Brazil floods. 95%+ long-term target amid favorable markets.

Capital deployment: $18.5 billion deployable, $4.2 billion surplus over 500% RBC. Acquisitions: Closed $2.8 billion Nexus Cyber ($450 million GWP, 88% ratio, +12% EPS, cyber to $2.1 billion); $3-5 billion 2025 tuck-ins—MGA Florida/California, Singapore embedded 40% stake $750 million Grab-like, UK health reinsurer $1.5 billion. New products: $1.1 billion R&D—Global Shield Parametric 2.0 $500 million climate with Planet Labs (95% NPS Australia), CyberGuard Elite blockchain SMEs, VitalLink Fitbit life Q1 2025, AssureAI 70% underwriting -1.8 points expenses. Returns: $4 billion buybacks (2.1% YTD), 2.8% dividend +10%, 60% FCF. 550% RBC post, $78.42 BVPS +12%. ROE 14-16% FY25.

Lisa Patel: Thank you, Michael. I'd like to provide an update on our underwriting performance. We've seen continued strong performance in our commercial P&C lines. We are actively managing our exposure to catastrophe risks like wildfires and hurricanes, and have implemented several initiatives to improve our risk selection, including the Zenith Nexus AI platform for faster, more accurate quoting and telematics in auto for better frequency control.

David Kim: Thank you. From an investment perspective, we have continued to focus on diversifying our portfolio and managing risk in the current market environment. With $285 billion in invested assets up 4% YoY, our allocation is 72% fixed income ($205 billion: 28% Treasuries/MBS at 4.6% yield 7.2 duration, 42% IG corporates 5.1% financials/utilities, 18% structured 5.8% non-agency RMBS/private CLOs, 12% HY/EM 7.2%), 15% public equities ($43 billion: 60% U.S. large-cap ETFs 8% YTD, 25% int'l developed, 15% EM), 13% alts ($37 billion: 40% PE 12% IRR Blackstone/KKR healthcare/software, 35% real assets 6.2-7.5% Sunbelt RE/infra renewables, 25% hedge 9%). Book yield 4.85% +25 bps, ALM AI optimizer. Fixed stable for L&A 12.5-year duration; equities beta 0.75 P&C surplus; alts illiquidity premia private credit $8 billion Ares/Apollo SOFR+450. Guide 70-75% fixed 2025, alts 15%, 5.5% yield. RBC 520%, AA- quality.

Robert Hayes: I'd like to briefly address our claims performance. We've implemented several initiatives to streamline our claims process and improve customer satisfaction, including AI-powered portals with Guidewire that cut processing times by 38% and digitized bordereaux reducing disputes. We are seeing positive results in terms of reduced claims processing times and higher NPS scores.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator: Thank you. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Jamie Carter with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Jamie Carter: Good morning. Can you provide more color on the premium growth outlook and how tech is influencing retention?

Sarah Thompson: Good morning, Jamie. Absolutely. As Michael detailed, we're guiding 7-9% full-year 2024 net premium growth, with Q4 at 5-7%. Tech like our AI underwriting on Google Cloud and DriveSafe telematics is key—cutting manual reviews 40%, boosting quote-to-bind 25%, and lifting retention to 90.5% with 20% account rounding. Embedded partnerships add $500 million ARP visibility. We're prioritizing quality over volume for 14%+ ROE.

Operator: Our next question comes from Emily Rodriguez with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Emily Rodriguez: Good morning. Could you discuss the impact of rising interest rates on your investment portfolio and unrealized positions?

Michael Chen: Good morning, Emily. Rates to 4.75% drove Q3 unrealized losses of $325 million, but our total return was 2.1% beating benchmarks, with realized gains $178 million from tactical trims. YTD NII up 12% on 5.1% reinvests. Derivatives hedge 40% equity duration, alts shift $10 billion private credit mitigates. Expect troughing losses and acceleration ahead with potential cuts.

Operator: Our next question comes from Tom Nguyen with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Tom Nguyen: Thanks. What is the expected impact of reinsurance renewals and cat activity on your combined ratio guidance?

Lisa Patel: Hi Tom. Our 1/1/25 renewals cede 25% after $500 million at 32% commissions, shielding tails despite soft pricing. Q4 cat guide $200-250 million 6-8 points, but ex-CAT mid-62s with reserves and social inflation slowdown. Nexus AI adds 1-2 points improvement; overall 96.5-98.5% confident.

Operator: Our next question from Laura Bennett with Barclays.

Laura Bennett: Good morning. Thoughts on CAC trends and how they tie to LTV in personal lines?

Michael Chen: Morning, Laura. CAC down 7.2% to $312 blended, personal 12% to $185 via 62% digital and UBI telematics—LTV:CAC 4.8x. GenAI personalization and embedded channels target sub-$300 by year-end, expanding to 4.2x overall with 88% retention.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] That covers our questions for now.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you for your questions and your interest in Zenith Insurance Group. In closing, we are confident in our ability to continue delivering strong results and creating value for our shareholders. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
